THE HEAVY LIFTER

Cargo plane.

When the payload is the priority, the airplane becomes a flying link in a much larger supply chain.

Family
Powered fixed-wing
Propulsion

OverviewKey featuresHow it worksCommon usesQuestions
01 / THE BIG PICTURE

Meet the cargo plane.

A cargo plane is designed or configured to carry freight. Cargo is a mission category rather than a single airframe layout: freighters range from small propeller aircraft to large jet transports, including converted passenger airplanes.

SPOT IT IN THE SKY

Look for large cargo doors, fewer cabin windows, and loading equipment. Some dedicated transports have high wings or a rear ramp; many converted airliners do not.

02 / DESIGN DETAILS

What makes it different.

01

Large loading access

Cargo doors, and on some designs ramps, allow bulky loads to enter the aircraft.

02

Load-bearing floor

Cargo compartments are designed for their specified floor loads and handling equipment.

03

Restraint systems

Pallet locks, nets, or other approved restraints secure freight during flight.

04

Mission-specific fuselage

Some freighters use a wide or tall body to accommodate loads that would not fit in a passenger cabin.

03 / HOW IT WORKS

The engineering
behind the flight.

The flight principles are the same as for other powered airplanes: engines provide thrust and wings provide lift. Cargo loading adds another important consideration. Load planners keep the aircraft within weight and balance limits and secure freight so it cannot shift.

Explore the four forces of flight ↗
04 / IN THE REAL WORLD

Made for a mission.

  • Express parcels and commercial freight
  • Transporting machinery and oversized equipment
  • Humanitarian supplies and relief logistics
CAPABILITIES & TRADEOFFS

Air freight offers speed and access over long distances, but is often more expensive than surface transport. Payload, range, cargo dimensions, and runway capability all depend on the particular aircraft.

05 / A CLOSER LOOK

Good questions.

Are all cargo planes large jets?

No. Cargo aircraft include small propeller planes, regional turboprops, and large jets.

Can a passenger plane become a freighter?

Some aircraft can be converted through an approved modification program, often involving structural changes, cargo access, and loading systems.

This guide describes an aircraft category. Equipment, speed, range, capacity, and operating limitations vary by model and configuration. Categories can overlap: a propeller aircraft can also be a cargo plane or seaplane.
